newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks likely to remain on bull run.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks likely to remain on bull run.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to head higher on Tuesday, as the recent bullish trend would be reinforced by the surge on Wall Street on Monday and stable currencies, brokers said.

On Friday, the 225-share Nikkei average rose 239.42 points or 1.24 percent to end at 19,514.75, a new closing high for 1997. June Nikkei futures closed 230 points higher at 19,530. Tokyo financial markets were closed on Monday for a holiday.
"The Nikkei 225 is likely to keep rising this week until it hits 20,000," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager of the equities operations group at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
Brokers expected the Nikkei 225 average on Tuesday to jump without much hesitation to 19,890, the level where Nikkei futures closed in Chicago on Monday.
But any rise in the key index might slow temporarily between 19,890 and 19,900 due to profit-taking, brokers said.
On Monday, the Dow industrials surged 143 points or two percent to 7214, an all-time closing high.
"The buying spree in New York will encourage investors to buy Japanese stocks," said a market analyst at a second-tier Japanese securities house.
